title: Isolation and Purification of BETALAINS Pigment from Celosia argentea and Beta vulgaris
author: Antonino M Lecona
materials: The supernatant liquid is filtered through a 0.2 µM nylon membrane (Millipore Corp., Bedford, MA) under vacuum at a temperature of 22°C.

steps.title: Prepare Plant Material
steps.instruction: Wash freshly collected plant material (Celosia argentea flowers or Beta vulgaris roots) thoroughly three times with sterile water and cut into small pieces (1 cm²), ensuring the process is conducted in darkness.

steps.title: Grind Frozen Samples
steps.instruction: Thoroughly grind frozen samples in a mortar until the tissue appears colorless, which takes approximately 20 minutes.

steps.title: Extract Betalains
steps.instruction: Extract pigments from the tissue using a methanol-ascorbate solution and collect the filtrate.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 ml/gram (fresh weight) of freshly prepared 80% methanol + 50 mM ascorbate to the tissue and continue grinding.
Collect the filtered solution in a 15 ml Falcon tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge Extract
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 14,000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4°C.

steps.title: Collect Supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant. If any signs of tissue contamination are observed in the sample, repeat the extraction and centrifugation steps.

steps.title: Prepare LH-20 Separation Column
steps.instruction: Prepare the LH-20 separation column using methanol as the solvent, maintaining a ratio of 3.9 ml for every 4.3 g of Sephadex column granules.

steps.title: Elute Pigments
steps.instruction: Transfer samples into the LH-20 separation column (100 x 2.5 cm diameter) and elute using water adjusted to a pH between 5 and 6 with formic acid.

steps.title: Collect and Store Phases
steps.instruction: Collect the phases from the separation columns separately for individual evaluation. Store filtrates at 4°C until required.

steps.title: Quantify Betalain Content
steps.instruction: Quantify the betalain content photometrically using the respective molar extinction coefficients at specific wavelengths.
